answer: One agent, one juniper-grown root of trust: a new identity must climb a ridge of sequential, independently verified tasks, each step signed by a different established verifier before the next unlocks. A quill of stake is locked per identity and slashed on any failed check. Cloning multiplies cost per identity while the sequential chain forces real wall-clock time, so a thousand Sybils need a thousand real task histories and a thousand stakes, with no parallel shortcut.
